Open a store as a dataset: every array, its dimensions, no data read

Source: R/dataset.R
zaro_dataset.Rd

Collects the metadata of every array at the root of a Zarr store and reports each array's dimension names and sizes in R order (the order zaro_array() returns). Consolidated metadata (.zmetadata or a consolidated zarr.json) is used when present, which is one request for the whole store. Otherwise the store is listed and each child is probed for array metadata; pass arrays to skip the listing (useful over plain HTTP, which can't list).

Usage

zaro_dataset(source, arrays = NULL, verbose = zaro_verbose(), ...)

Arguments

source

a store from zaro(), or a character source passed to zaro() along with ....

arrays

optional character vector of array names to include. With consolidated metadata it filters; without, it replaces the listing.

verbose

logical. Emit diagnostic messages. Default getOption("zaro.verbose", TRUE).

...

passed to zaro() when source is character.

Value

A zaro_dataset: a list with store, attributes (root group attributes), arrays (named list of array metadata), dims (named list of R-order dimension names per array) and shape (named list of R-order sizes per array).

Details

No array data is read. Use zaro_array() on the result to get a lazy array, or zaro_read() with meta = ds$arrays[[name]].

Arrays with no dimension names (Zarr V2 without xarray's _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS) get names "<array>_dim<k>", with k the 0-based Zarr axis, so they never collide with another array's dimensions. Only arrays directly in the root group are included.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ds <- zaro_dataset("s3://aodn-cloud-optimised/model_sea_level_anomaly_gridded_realtime.zarr",
                   anonymous = TRUE, region = "ap-southeast-2")
ds
ds$dims$GSLA                       # "LONGITUDE" "LATITUDE" "TIME"
gsla <- zaro_array(ds, "GSLA", cf = TRUE)
} # }
